26.​Add after paragraph 94 and renumber (Chelmsford) 
 
As Reform scale down their anti-establishment rhetoric they become vulnerable to 
being outflanked to the right. The recently founded 'Restore Britain' party, led by the 
ex-Reform MP Rupert Lowe, has recognised this opportunity and is proposing a slew 
of far-right policies such as remigration, further targeting of the Islamic community 
with bans on the burqa and Halal meat, and the reintroduction of the death penalty. 
According to Restore themselves, the party has achieved a membership of 100,000 
people less than two weeks after being founded. The impact that this party could have 
on the Reform party's electoral success remains to be seen.​
 
CC recommendation: Reject  
 
27.​Add after paragraph 120 and renumber (Chelmsford) 
 
Unite has cut its annual funding to Labour by 40% in response to the party’s handling 
of the Birmingham bin strike, and the question of disaffiliation will be posed at Unite’s 
2027 rules conference. This shows the disdain that workers currently have for the 
Labour party. However, without a viable political alternative, the left union leaders are 
unable or unwilling to seize upon this energy. For now they remain in semi-opposition 
to the Labour party. 
​
CC recommendation: Reject  
 
28.​Amend paragraph 122 (Manchester - Withington 2)  
 
The TUC has further cocooned itself by farming out campaigning responsibilities to broad ad 
hoc campaigns such as Stand Up To Racism, Stop the War, the People’s Assembly, etc. 
This provides sectarians such as the SWP and the CPB with funds and an air of legitimacy, 
while allowing the TUC bureaucrats to put their official stamp on things whilst doing nothing 
in practice. This alphabet soup of left reformism and sectarianism is ineffective and 
off-putting to most workers. It must be said that the radicalised youth are no longer 
looking toward the trade unions to improve their conditions. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject
